method: Use plain, uncoated oven-ready chips without batter. Preheat the oven to the temperature on the oven-chips packet, commonly 220°C conventional or 200°C fan; use the packet setting if different. Spread enough oven chips on a tray in one layer to provide a 250g cooked portion, without adding extra oil, and bake for the packet time, usually about 20–30 minutes, turning halfway. They should be crisp and golden rather than dark brown. Weigh out 250g after cooking for this serving; the ingredient amount and nutrition use cooked chip weight.

Slice the red onion and mixed peppers thinly. Heat half of the measured olive oil in a non-stick frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened with a little colour; transfer to a clean bowl.
Mix the measured light mayonnaise and tomato ketchup in a clean small bowl. Keep this finishing sauce separate from the uncooked filling and refrigerated until assembly.

Cut the lean pork loin across the grain into strips about 1cm thick. Coat with all the measured paprika and chilli powder. After handling raw lean pork loin, wash hands and clean the board, knife and work surface before touching the ready-to-eat ingredients.

Add the remaining half of the measured olive oil to the non-stick frying pan. Cook the pork strips over a medium-high heat for about 7–9 minutes, turning regularly. Check the centre with a clean food thermometer: it must stay at 75°C or above for 30 seconds. Without a thermometer, cut the thickest piece open and check that it is steaming inside with no pink meat and the juices are clear. Continue cooking until these checks are met; the suggested pan time alone is not a safety check.
Return the cooked red onion and mixed peppers to the pan for 1–2 minutes, turning gently until hot.

Pile the crisp oven chips onto a plate and spoon over the cooked pork strips, the red onion and peppers. Drizzle the cold finishing sauce over the top after cooking. Serve immediately while the chips are crisp.
